title: Always-on AI agent cost calculator: laptop, server or cloud
h1: what does it really cost to keep an ai agent running?
description: A free calculator: what a month of keeping AI bots running costs on a spare computer, a rented server or dusk cloud, once your own time counts.
keywords: vps vs cloud for ai agents
answer: the server is rarely the expensive part. your time is. a spare computer costs a few dollars of power a month, a small server costs whatever your host charges, and both cost you every evening spent on updates and restarts. dusk cloud is a flat $20 or $50 a month and we do the upkeep. put your own numbers in below and see which one wins for you.

review.by: lead agent, rewritten by hand in the new voice; arithmetic checked

og_line: laptop, spare computer, server or cloud.
method:
**electricity is cheap. it's almost never the deciding number.**

a spare computer idling all month:

```text
watts / 1,000 = kilowatts
x hours on per day
x 30.4 days in an average month
x your price per kwh
= your monthly power bill for it

20 w, 24 h, $0.20: 0.02 x 24 x 30.4 x 0.20 = about $2.92
```

**your time is the big one.** updates, a restart after a power cut, a backup you forgot to check. one hour a month at $40 an hour already costs more than the power and most small servers.

**a rented server is its bill plus that same time.** Metal is free to run on [your own server](/docs/your-own-server). it needs ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 and 2 gb of memory or more.

**dusk cloud is flat.** plus is $20 a month or $200 a year. pro is $50 a month or $500 a year. we keep the machine running and back it up every day ([pricing](/pricing)).

left out on purpose:

- buying the spare computer in the first place
- your internet bill
- your ai plan, which every option uses and your ai provider bills

sections.md:
**if you only use bots at your desk, the free row wins.** stay on your laptop. no shame in it.

**the other rows only matter when you want things to happen without you.** the morning brief at 7, a reply from your phone at midnight, a long job that finishes while you sleep.

**then compare with your time switched on.** a $5 server that eats an evening a month isn't a $5 server. most people who run their own box underprice their evenings.

want the full picture of each option, not just the money? read [where ai agents run when your laptop is closed](/agents-when-laptop-closed).

steps: type your electricity price from your last bill
guess the hours a month you'd spend on upkeep
put a price on one of those hours
look at the row that's cheapest with your time in

mistakes.fix: even $20 an hour changes the answer. be honest with yourself.

mistakes.mistake: using the watts on the power brick
mistakes.fix: that's the maximum. idle draw is much lower: check the spec sheet or a plug-in meter.
a bot working all night uses your ai plan all night. that bill doesn't change with where the bot lives.

tip.text: a bot that runs around the clock uses your ai plan around the clock. for heavy use, a bigger plan or an api key is the cheaper route.

faq.q: where do the starting numbers come from?
faq.a: they're examples, not measurements. your real watts are on the computer's spec sheet or a plug-in meter. your real power price is on your bill.

faq.q: does the calculator send my numbers anywhere?
faq.a: no. it runs in your browser and sends nothing.
